meta.coordinate_note: origin top-left, x increases left to right; route order is right to left (descending x)

hotspots.title: A Collector's Shelf Mark?
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 「卷首有千字文第七四二「慮」字編號，卷末有項氏「價值兩百金」語」
Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 38 and Fig. 3 — 「卷首下方並註記千字文「慮」字號，拖尾末端書寫「子孫永寶，值價貳佰金」小字」
hotspots.reason: Character is sharp at native size; both sources agree; unique ownership story.
hotspots.story_en: In the bottom corner, beside the red seals, sits one small ink character: 慮. The museum reads it as collector Xiang Yuanbian's inventory number, counted off from the Thousand Character Classic. Even a painted palace, it seems, needed a shelf mark.
hotspots.fact_zh: 卷首右下角墨书「慮」字，为项元汴以《千字文》编号的收藏号（故宫著录：第七四二字）。「值价贰佰金」写在拖尾，本母版不含拖尾，故卡片不展示价格。
hotspots.visible: A single black ink character 慮 about 65 px tall on the painted silk, right of a square red seal and below a gourd-shaped seal, at the right edge of the painting.
hotspots.guardrail: Say only what is visible: the character. The price note is on the tail paper, which is not in this master; do not show or locate it.
hotspots.open_issues: Rubric feared a discrepancy between sources. Checked: catalogue and Xu agree on 慮 and on 200 gold (wording differs: 價值兩百金 vs 值價貳佰金). Subject is small; needs the spotlight crop.

hotspots.title: A Swing with Nobody on It?
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45 and Fig. 12 — 「畫家以晨霧中空無一人的鞦韆，作為一幅宮廷仕女圖的序曲」
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 鞦韆
hotspots.reason: Unmistakable, sourced to a figure, and the natural first stop.
hotspots.story_en: Before any palace lady appears, a red swing stands empty in the morning mist. Scholar Xu Wenmei links it to old palace poems, where swings belong to the spring festival season. The scroll announces spring without showing a single person.
hotspots.fact_zh: 卷首柳烟中空无一人的秋千。许文美指出其呼应宫词「寒食鞦韆滿地時」，以寒食秋千暗示春季。
hotspots.visible: Two red poles with pennants, a slanting red crossbar and thin hanging ropes with no rider, rising behind misty willows.
hotspots.guardrail: No rider is shown; do not invent one or name a specific Han festival event.
hotspots.open_issues: None.

hotspots.title: A Rock Worth Admiring?
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 奇石; 「林木奇石與華麗的宮闕穿插掩映」
hotspots.reason: Very legible; fills the stretch between swing and gate.
hotspots.story_en: Outside the wall stands a tall grey rock, full of holes and hollows, with pink blossoms growing around it. Rocks like this were prized in Chinese gardens for their strange shapes. The stranger the stone, the better the view.
hotspots.fact_zh: 宫墙外的奇石（湖石状，多孔洞），周围有粉色花。故宫著录主题列「奇石」，简介称「林木奇石與華麗的宮闕穿插掩映」。
hotspots.visible: A grey, perforated, upright rock about 1,000 px wide with small pink-flowered shrubs at its base, next to the tiled wall.
hotspots.guardrail: Do not name the stone type, a quarry or a specific specimen.
hotspots.open_issues: 'Prized for strange shapes' is general garden-history knowledge, not a statement in the two core sources; keep it general.

hotspots.title: Through the Palace Gate
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45 — 「接續著半開的宮門、城牆、和御溝」; p. 53 — 「仇英憑藉自身具備高超的界畫技巧」
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 技法: 界畫
hotspots.reason: Merges gate and jiehua into one strong, sourced architectural stop.
hotspots.story_en: A red gate stands ajar, and behind it roofs, walls and railings run on in perfectly straight lines. This ruled-line style is called jiehua, and Qiu Ying was a master of it. The palace is imaginary; the geometry is exact.
hotspots.fact_zh: 半开的宫门与宫墙。许文美：柳树秋千之后「接續著半開的宮門、城牆、和御溝」；并称仇英「具備高超的界畫技巧」。故宫著录技法列「界畫」。
hotspots.visible: A red gateway with two white-capped posts and one slatted door leaf, set in an orange wall with green-and-blue tiled roofs drawn in ruled parallel lines.
hotspots.guardrail: Imagined architecture; do not present it as the layout of a real Han palace.
hotspots.open_issues: H02 and H21 merged: one architectural story is enough.

hotspots.title: A Duck on the Railing?
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 翎毛 鴛鴦
hotspots.reason: Adds a natural detail and a stop in the quiet pond stretch.
hotspots.story_en: One small bird perches on the stone railing above the pond, with a red bill and a sweep of orange and white. The museum's catalogue names mandarin ducks among the painting's birds. Easy to miss; hard to forget once found.
hotspots.fact_zh: 池边石栏上的一只鸳鸯（雄）。故宫著录翎毛列「鴛鴦」。
hotspots.visible: A small duck with red bill, white eye-stripe, orange-brown cheek and chest, perched on a railing post; about 80 x 160 px.
hotspots.guardrail: One bird only; no 'pair' symbolism.
hotspots.open_issues: Bird confirmed at native size: red bill, white eye-stripe, orange-brown cheek, pale breast, i.e. a drake mandarin duck. Small (about 80 x 160 px): needs the spotlight crop. Promoted by the owner's decision, 2026-11-09.

hotspots.title: A Peacock in the Palace?
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 46, Figs. 14 and 24 — 「孔雀…因絢麗嬌貴豢養於宮禁之中，也為其他宮詞作品關注描寫」
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 孔雀
hotspots.reason: Top-tier: large, vivid, figure-referenced.
hotspots.story_en: Two peacocks stroll across the courtyard while ladies lean from a window to watch. Peacocks turn up in old palace poetry, kept for their dazzling feathers; one verse even imagines the plumes sewn into a dance costume.
hotspots.fact_zh: 庭中两只孔雀，窗内仕女探身观看（许文美列为「賞鳥」）。许引敦煌本《宮詞叢鈔》：「孔雀知恩無意飛，開籠任性在宮闈，裁人亦見輕羅錦，欲取金毛繡舞衣。」
hotspots.visible: Two blue-green peafowl on the pavement, one with a long eyed train; above them two women and a fan-bearer look out of a lattice window.
hotspots.guardrail: No owner, import route or symbolism. The poem is poetry, not a record of this court.
hotspots.open_issues: H05 bird-watching folded in here (Xu's Fig. 14 is this same scene).

hotspots.title: The Palace Garden Had Work to Do
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 器用 花器 澆花器; 簡介「琴棋書畫、鑑古、蒔花等文人的休閒活動」
hotspots.reason: Clear action that matches a specific catalogue term.
hotspots.story_en: Beside the great rock, a woman tips a long-necked vessel over the flowering shrubs. Others in this courtyard pick blossoms and admire them; she is the one keeping them alive. The museum's catalogue even lists her tool: a flower-watering vessel.
hotspots.fact_zh: 奇石花圃旁，一女子倾长颈器浇花。故宫著录主题列「花器／澆花器」，简介提及「蒔花」。
hotspots.visible: A woman bending forward, holding a mauve long-necked vessel mouth-down over leafy shrubs with pink flowers in a stone-edged bed around a tall brown rock.
hotspots.guardrail: Do not name her job or the plant species.
hotspots.open_issues: No water is drawn; 'watering' rests on the pose plus the catalogue term.

hotspots.title: Spring Is in the Details
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45 and Fig. 15 — 賞花
hotspots.reason: Figure-referenced and clearly an interaction with flowers, not just a tree.
hotspots.story_en: A lady reaches up to break off a flowering branch while her attendant waits with a tray. Flower-viewing is one of the palace pastimes Xu Wenmei traces through the scroll and through the poems behind it. Somebody, of course, has to carry the flowers.
hotspots.fact_zh: 仕女折花，侍女捧盘相随。许文美将此段列为「賞花」（图15）。
hotspots.visible: A woman in a red shawl with one arm raised to a branch of a white-flowering tree; a smaller figure in blue beside her holds a shallow tray.
hotspots.guardrail: No flower species, no month.
hotspots.open_issues: Overlaps in theme with the optional flower-in-hair moment 1,300 px to the right; keep only one unless you want both.

hotspots.title: Getting Ready for the Day
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45 and Fig. 13 — 「足見「曉妝」是宮詞的重要母題，畫作由此蘊含「春曉」的畫意」
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 銅鏡．奩
hotspots.reason: Explains the title itself.
hotspots.story_en: Under a leafy tree, a woman lifts both hands to fix her hair before a mirror on a red table. 'Morning adornment' is a favourite scene in palace poetry, and it gives the scroll its mood: spring, dawn, and not quite ready yet.
hotspots.fact_zh: 晨起梳妆：女子对镜理发，红案上置镜台与妆奁。许文美：「曉妝」是宫词的重要母题，画作由此蕴含「春曉」的画意。
hotspots.visible: A seated woman with both arms raised to her hair, facing a mirror stand and boxes on a low red table; a second woman kneels opposite.
hotspots.guardrail: No cosmetics recipes; not evidence of Han cosmetics.
hotspots.open_issues: None.

hotspots.title: A Dance Before the Music Ends?
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 46 and Fig. 16 — 「畫作中眾多宮女從事的樂、舞活動…原為抒寫宮女才情的重要母題」
hotspots.reason: Clear poses; figure-referenced.
hotspots.story_en: Two dancers turn toward each other, long blue sleeves flying, while the musicians play a few steps away. Music and dance fill the old palace poems, which praised court women for their talents. Here the poem becomes a performance.
hotspots.fact_zh: 两名舞者相对起舞，旁为乐队。许文美：乐、舞为宫词「抒寫宮女才情的重要母題」（图16）。
hotspots.visible: Two women in blue jackets and white skirts, arms extended and sleeves trailing, facing each other at the edge of the music hall.
hotspots.guardrail: No dance title, repertoire or dancer identity.
hotspots.open_issues: None.

hotspots.title: Pipa or Zheng?
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 樂器 琵琶．箏．琴．排簫．笛．箜篌
Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., Fig. 16 (演奏樂器)
hotspots.reason: Both instruments legible in one crop; the bridges make the distinction checkable.
hotspots.story_en: Two string instruments, two shapes. The pear-shaped one held upright is a pipa. The long one on the red stand, with a row of small bridges under its strings, is a zheng. Behind it, a woman seems to be pulling a string tight.
hotspots.fact_zh: 琵琶（梨形、竖抱）与筝（置红架上，弦下可见一排雁柱）。故宫著录乐器列「琵琶．箏．琴…」。筝后绿衣女子似在上弦。
hotspots.visible: A seated woman holding a pear-shaped lute with a decorated belly; a long narrow instrument on a red trestle with small triangular bridges; a standing woman in green pulling red cords at its end.
hotspots.guardrail: The zheng is identified by its visible bridges; do not call it a qin. The stringing action is my reading: keep 'seems'.
hotspots.open_issues: H16 and H17 merged.

hotspots.title: Who Is Napping Up There?
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 走獸 貓（貍奴）
hotspots.reason: The most playful find; passes only with the tight crop and the honest wording.
hotspots.story_en: Above the musicians, on a round stool with a red cushion, something small and fluffy is curled up fast asleep. A cat? A lapdog? The museum's catalogue lists a cat among this painting's subjects, so that is our best guess. Concert or no concert, it is not getting up.
hotspots.fact_zh: 乐队上方藤墩红垫上蜷睡的小兽。故宫著录「走獸」项仅列「貓（貍奴）」。
hotspots.visible: A small cream-and-tan long-haired animal curled asleep on a red cushion on a woven round stool, behind the hall's columns; about 150 x 80 px.
hotspots.guardrail: No name, owner or breed. The card must not assert that this animal is the catalogue's cat; it offers it as the best guess.
hotspots.open_issues: The long fur and flat face could also read as a lapdog. The catalogue lists a cat and no dog, and this is the only such animal I found in the whole scroll, so the match is by elimination. Small subject: needs a tight spotlight crop.

hotspots.title: Unwrapping the Qin
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 簡介「琴棋書畫」; 主題: 樂器 琴
hotspots.reason: An unusual, readable action that carries the 'scholar's arts' idea.
hotspots.story_en: Two women slide a long black instrument out of its patterned cloth cover. It is a qin, the zither of Chinese scholars; the museum notes that this scroll gives its palace ladies the scholar's pastimes of qin, chess, calligraphy and painting.
hotspots.fact_zh: 两女子自锦囊中抽出黑色长琴。故宫简介：「復融入琴棋書畫、鑑古、蒔花等文人的休閒活動」。
hotspots.visible: A long, narrow black instrument held level by one woman while another pulls a dark gold-patterned cloth sleeve off its end; a tea or wine table stands beside them.
hotspots.guardrail: Identified as a qin by shape (long, narrow, black, no bridges). Do not name a piece of music.
hotspots.open_issues: None.

hotspots.title: A Game with Grass?
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45 and Fig. 17 — 鬥草; pp. 48-49
hotspots.reason: Figure-referenced; the plants in the hands are visible.
hotspots.story_en: A small group sits in a circle on the ground, holding out sprigs and flowers; more lie scattered beside them. Xu Wenmei identifies the game as doucao, a springtime contest played with plants. Who is winning? The painting is not telling.
hotspots.fact_zh: 席地围坐、手持花草相较，地上散落花枝。许文美定为「鬥草」（图17），并认为此段可能参考〈宮中圖〉席地而坐的宫女姿态。
hotspots.visible: Three seated women and a child seen from behind, hands extended toward the centre holding small plants; loose sprigs and petals on the ground to the right.
hotspots.guardrail: No rules, no winner.
hotspots.open_issues: None.

hotspots.title: A Quiet Corner for Reading
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45 and Fig. 18 — 讀書
hotspots.reason: Clear book, clear pose.
hotspots.story_en: Two women lie side by side on a flowered rug, chins on their arms, sharing one open book. A long zither rests beside them. Xu Wenmei counts reading among the scroll's palace pastimes: learning, pictured as pure leisure.
hotspots.fact_zh: 两女子伏卧花毯同读一册，身旁置琴。许文美列为「讀書」（图18）。
hotspots.visible: Two women lying prone on a green rug patterned with peonies, an open book in front of them, a book stand to the left and a long black zither along the rug's edge.
hotspots.guardrail: Do not name the book.
hotspots.open_issues: None.

hotspots.title: A Parrot Among the Courtiers?
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 46 and Fig. 23 — 「珍禽如鸚鵡」; appendix, 朱慶餘〈宮中詞〉
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 鸚鵡
hotspots.reason: Sourced to a figure plus a memorable verse.
hotspots.story_en: On the red railing sits a small green parrot, and two women have stopped to look. Parrots turn up again and again in palace poems; one famous line says the ladies dare not gossip in front of the bird.
hotspots.fact_zh: 红栏上的绿鹦鹉，两仕女驻足。许文美：鹦鹉（图23）在三部《宮詞》中皆有描述；附录引朱慶餘〈宮中詞〉「含情欲説宮中事，鸚鵡前頭不敢言」。
hotspots.visible: A green long-tailed bird with a red bill perched on a red rail; two women stand close together at the left, looking toward it. The bird is uncaged.
hotspots.guardrail: Perched and uncaged, as drawn. No claim that it talks.
hotspots.open_issues: The rubric assigned Fig. 23 to geese/ducks; in the article Fig. 23 is the parrot. The bird is about 150 px long: needs the spotlight crop.

hotspots.title: A Move on the Go Board
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45 and Fig. 19 — 下棋
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — English description: 'the zither, chess, calligraphy, and painting'
hotspots.reason: Board and stones are legible.
hotspots.story_en: Around a low table, players lean over a gridded board dotted with black and white stones while friends crowd in to watch. The game is weiqi, known in English as Go. An attendant with a tall fan stands by.
hotspots.fact_zh: 围棋：格线棋盘上可见黑白子，旁有观者与执扇侍者。许文美列为「下棋」（图19）。
hotspots.visible: A square board with a ruled grid and round stones on a low black table; four women seated or leaning around it; a standing attendant holding a long-handled blue fan.
hotspots.guardrail: Go is my identification from the gridded board with stones on it. Say nothing about the position or who is winning.
hotspots.open_issues: The rubric says the museum's English text 'explicitly mentions Go'; the catalogue text I read says 'chess' (棋). Xu also compares the group's composition with a painting of double-sixes players, which concerns the grouping, not the game.

hotspots.title: Children in a Palace Painting?
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45, Fig. 20-1; p. 50 comparison with 傳周昉〈戲嬰圖〉 (Fig. 50)
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 孩童
hotspots.reason: Figure-referenced.
hotspots.story_en: A woman lifts a baby in a red jacket while a toddler crawls at her knees, and another lady looks on from the stairs. 'Playing with infants' is one of the pastimes scholars list in this scroll, with roots in much older paintings of court women.
hotspots.fact_zh: 戏婴：女子抱红衣婴儿，另一幼儿伏地，阶旁一女子旁观。许文美列为「戲嬰」（图20-1），并与传周昉〈戲嬰圖〉比较。
hotspots.visible: A seated woman holding up an infant in red; a second small child in green on all fours; a woman in green seated on a staircase rail to the right.
hotspots.guardrail: No names, no mother-and-child claim.
hotspots.open_issues: A second infant scene (Fig. 20-2) is listed as optional.

hotspots.title: Threads, Needles, and Patience
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 45 and Fig. 21 — 織繡; p. 49 comparison with 〈紈扇仕女圖〉
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 織（刺繡．女紅用具．針．線）
hotspots.reason: Figure-referenced.
hotspots.story_en: One woman pulls a thread high, another bends close over a long embroidery frame, and a third rests her chin on her hand. Needlework is on the museum's list of subjects for this scroll, tools included. Patience, apparently, came in different amounts.
hotspots.fact_zh: 织绣：一人引线，一人伏绷架刺绣，一人支颐。许文美列为「織繡」（图21）；故宫著录「織（刺繡．女紅用具．針．線）」。
hotspots.visible: A long frame with dark blue cloth and pink flower motifs; a woman behind it with both hands raised holding thread; a woman in front bending over the cloth; a third leaning on a red table.
hotspots.guardrail: Embroidery, not weaving or reeling; no stitch names.
hotspots.open_issues: Sits directly above the ironing scene (same x): two markers stacked vertically.

hotspots.title: Ironing, Palace Style
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 49, Figs. 41-42 — 熨衣一段與〈搗練圖〉熨衣段落類似
hotspots.reason: Strong art-historical insight with an everyday hook.
hotspots.story_en: Women stretch a length of white silk between them while one presses it with a pan of glowing coals: an iron. Xu Wenmei notes that the group closely echoes a famous older painting of court ladies preparing silk. Qiu Ying knew his classics.
hotspots.fact_zh: 熨衣：白练拉平，以盛炭火的熨斗熨烫。许文美：「〈漢宮春曉〉熨衣一段（圖42）與〈搗練圖〉熨衣段落類似」。
hotspots.visible: A long white cloth pulled taut by a woman at the left; a woman in red rests a shallow pan with red coals on it; a woman in blue bends at the right.
hotspots.guardrail: Say 'echoes', not 'copies'; do not date or attribute the older painting on the card.
hotspots.open_issues: Not in the rubric register; added because it is sourced and visually distinct.

hotspots.title: A Harp in a Chinese Palace?
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 48, Figs. 39-1 and 39-2
NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 樂器 箜篌
hotspots.reason: Distinct instrument, strong source.
hotspots.story_en: A lady plucks a tall, bow-shaped harp, the konghou, while her companion marks time with red clappers. Xu Wenmei shows that this pair was borrowed from a much older court painting. Qiu Ying was quoting a classic, almost figure for figure.
hotspots.fact_zh: 箜篌与拍板。许文美：彈奏箜篌一段选取〈宮中圖〉中「執拍板與彈箜篌的宮女」图式（图39-1、39-2）。
hotspots.visible: A seated woman with both hands on the strings of a tall curved harp with a decorated arm; facing her, a seated figure holding a fan of red slats.
hotspots.guardrail: Do not date the older painting on the card.
hotspots.open_issues: Not a separate rubric item; replaces a generic 'ensemble' card with a specific sourced one.

hotspots.title: Who Is Painting Whom?
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 「其中，並包含畫師毛延壽為王昭君寫像的著名故實」; second note: 「可知初無一定故事」
Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., pp. 39-40 (reviews Miyazaki Noriko 宮崎法子 2005 and Qin Xiaolei 秦曉磊), p. 46 and Fig. 22
hotspots.reason: The scroll's climax, told with the disagreement intact.
hotspots.story_en: A painter leans toward his picture; his sitter, in red, holds perfectly still. The museum has long linked the scene to the legend of Mao Yanshou painting the beauty Wang Zhaojun. Scholars have questioned that reading, and the museum's own notes admit the theme has no single fixed story. So who is she?
hotspots.fact_zh: 画师写像。故宫说明传统上释为毛延寿为王昭君写像；但故宫另一则说明亦称此题材「初無一定故事」。许文美综述了此前学者的质疑（宮崎法子2005年认为〈宮中圖〉与本卷似皆非以昭君故事为题材；秦曉磊指出「漢宮春曉」画题并非专画单一故事），并指出此段缺乏昭君故事的情节表现，可由宫词「宮女安排入畫圖」的传统来理解。
hotspots.visible: A bearded man seated on a stool painting a woman's face on an upright panel, colours on a low table beside him; at the left a seated woman in a red robe under a large round fan, with attendants.
hotspots.guardrail: Keep both readings. The doubt belongs to several scholars (Miyazaki Noriko 2005, Qin Xiaolei, discussed and extended by Xu Wenmei), not to Xu alone. The bribery tale is legend and stays off the card.
hotspots.open_issues: None.

hotspots.title: A Fan Raised High
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 草蟲 蝶蛾
hotspots.reason: A readable human moment in an otherwise empty stretch; the card asks a question instead of inventing an answer.
hotspots.story_en: A woman in red steps forward with a round fan raised high above her head, sleeves and sash flying. The museum's catalogue lists butterflies in this scroll, and two rest in the willows further left, but none is near her. What caught her eye? The painting leaves it open.
hotspots.fact_zh: 红衣女子举扇疾行，姿态似扑蝶，但其附近并无蝴蝶；两只蝴蝶在左侧约两千像素外的柳树上。故宫著录列「蝶蛾」。
hotspots.visible: A woman in a red jacket and white skirt in mid-stride, one arm raising a round fan above her head; open ground around her.
hotspots.guardrail: Describe only the gesture. Do not say she is catching a butterfly, where she is going or why she hurries.
hotspots.open_issues: Promoted by the owner's decision, 2026-11-09. Fills the long stretch between the portrait and the signature.

hotspots.title: The Artist Left His Name
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 款識: 仇英實父謹製; 印記: 實父, 仇英
Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., p. 38 and Fig. 2
hotspots.reason: Readable at native size; closes the journey.
hotspots.story_en: At the very end, in tiny characters down the edge: 'Respectfully made by Qiu Ying, Shifu,' with two small red seals. A Ming-dynasty painter signing a Han-dynasty palace that he imagined more than a thousand years after it stood.
hotspots.fact_zh: 卷末款「仇英實父謹製」，下钤「實父」「仇英」二印。仇英（约1494–1552）为明人，所画为想象中的汉宫。
hotspots.visible: A vertical line of six small black characters, 仇英實父謹製, followed by two small red seals, beside the large collector seals at the left edge of the silk.
hotspots.guardrail: Only the two small seals under the signature are Qiu Ying's; the large ones beside them are collectors'.
hotspots.open_issues: Removed from the app at the owner's request, 2026-11-09; kept here as an optional candidate. H24 (Ming painter, Han subject) was folded in here.

hotspots.title: What Is on the Table?
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 簡介「琴棋書畫、鑑古、蒔花」; 主題: 器用
hotspots.reason: Objects are clear, but the story is weaker than the rubric hoped: no group examining them.
hotspots.story_en: Through an open window: a patterned bronze vessel, a white bowl on its stand, a slim vase and stacks of books. The museum counts 'appreciating antiquities' among the scholar's pleasures that Qiu Ying gave to these palace women.
hotspots.fact_zh: 窗内案上陈设：铜器、白瓷碗、瓶、书函。故宫简介提及「鑑古」。
hotspots.visible: A red-legged table seen through a window, holding a lidded bronze-coloured vessel with a key-fret pattern, a white bowl on a red stand, a small vase and stacked books.
hotspots.guardrail: No dynasty or function for any object.
hotspots.open_issues: No one is shown inspecting the objects, so 'appreciating antiquities' is only loosely illustrated. Sits directly above the watering scene.

hotspots.title: A Flower for Your Hair
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., Fig. 15 area (賞花)
hotspots.reason: Charming and clear, but duplicates the flower theme.
hotspots.story_en: One woman reaches up to tuck a small blossom into her friend's hair. Just behind them, others are picking the branches. It is the quietest kind of spring ritual, and Qiu Ying gave it a corner of its own.
hotspots.fact_zh: 一女子为同伴簪花。属许文美「賞花」段的一部分。
hotspots.visible: Two standing women face to face; the one on the right raises her hand, holding a small sprig, to the other's hair.
hotspots.guardrail: No relationship between the two women.
hotspots.open_issues: Same theme as the accepted flower-picking card; a swap is possible if you prefer this one.

hotspots.title: Up You Come?
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., Fig. 20-2
hotspots.reason: Passes, but only one infant card is needed.
hotspots.story_en: A small child leans over the stair rail, held by a lady, while a girl below reaches up with both hands. Xu Wenmei places this among the scroll's scenes of playing with infants, a pastime older court paintings loved too.
hotspots.fact_zh: 阶上女子扶幼儿凭栏，阶下少女伸手相逗。许文美图20-2「戲嬰」。
hotspots.visible: A child with a shaved head leaning over a red stair rail with a woman behind; a figure in green below, back to the viewer, both arms raised toward the child.
hotspots.guardrail: No names or relationships.
hotspots.open_issues: Second infant scene; duplicates the accepted one.

hotspots.title: (brazier)
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 香爐．火盆
hotspots.reason: Object is clear but there is no sourced story beyond the catalogue word; third marker in the same hall.
hotspots.fact_zh: 女子以箸拨炭盆。
hotspots.visible: A kneeling woman holding two sticks over a low round pan of red coals.

hotspots.title: (two guards)
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 軍士
hotspots.reason: No source for who they are or what they are doing.
hotspots.fact_zh: 台阶下两名持杖男子。
hotspots.visible: Two men in dark robes and black caps, one holding a red staff, heads together.

hotspots.title: (attendants with trays)
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 飲食器
hotspots.reason: Contents of the trays cannot be named; no sourced story.
hotspots.fact_zh: 捧盘、执壶侍女。
hotspots.visible: Four women walking, carrying a tray of round items, a ewer and a covered vessel.

hotspots.title: (blue rock)
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 奇石
hotspots.reason: Any pigment or symbolism claim would be unsourced; the grey rock already tells the rock story.
hotspots.fact_zh: 青绿色湖石。
hotspots.visible: A tall perforated rock painted bright blue.

hotspots.title: (group with a pale panel)
hotspots.reason: Cannot tell what the panel is (painting, fan, screen). No one in the scroll is clearly drawing or writing apart from the portrait painter, so H19 has no valid anchor.
hotspots.fact_zh: 数人围看一素色板状物。
hotspots.visible: Seven women standing; one holds up a large pale four-sided panel.

hotspots.title: (woman on steps)
hotspots.reason: No source; purpose of the ewer unknown.
hotspots.fact_zh: 下阶女子持巾与壶。
hotspots.visible: A woman descending steps with a cloth in one hand and a gold-coloured ewer in the other.

hotspots.title: (window with fans and screen)
sources: NPM catalogue 故畫001038, https://digitalarchive.npm.gov.tw/Collection/Detail?dep=P&id=3672 — 主題: 后妃
hotspots.reason: The main figure is not visible; any identity would be invented. H24's point is carried by the signature card.
hotspots.fact_zh: 窗内障扇、龙纹屏风，主位人物被遮。
hotspots.visible: A window showing two blue ceremonial fans and a screen with dragons; the central seat's occupant is hidden.

hotspots.title: (200-gold inscription)
sources: Xu Wenmei 許文美, 〈宮中行樂—仇英〈漢宮春曉〉研究〉, 故宮學術季刊 36:1, pp. 37 ff., Fig. 3
hotspots.reason: Fails gate 1: the inscription is not in the chosen master. Dropped rather than given invented coordinates.
hotspots.fact_zh: 「子孫永寶，值價貳佰金」写于拖尾。
hotspots.visible: Not present: the master ends at the mounting silk left of the signature; the tail paper is not included.
